correctness.rationale: The residual is exactly the minimum-norm polynomial with two boundary value conditions (or a value and derivative at coincidence). The 2x2 Gram inverse and confluent moment inverse give exact finite expressions. Uniform critical scaling follows from finite uniform distributions and Riemann sums; geometric-sum bounds handle diverging scales. Half-angle factors locate all strict F<2 windows. The derivative W has W_prime=c^3 sin c-4(1-cos c)^2, and the monotone ratio argument proves one first-window minimum; a rigorous tail bound excludes every later window. Compactness then proves the exact global asymptotic optimum and all-minimizer rigidity. The bundled checker passed 10167 finite assertions; no infinite conclusion relies on finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The reported finite inverse-Gram formula is explicitly known from Bénéteau–Manolaki–Seco (2019), and the fixed-distinct-two-zero construction occurs in Acuaviva–Seco (2021/2022). Their statements were compared for logical implication. The final new claim is instead the sharp optimization over degree-dependent zero separation, including uniqueness of the global limiting minimizer, asymptotic rigidity of all optimizing separations, and an exact infinite family of beating intervals. No corresponding optimization statement was identified in the inspected full relevant sections or indexed search. This is best-knowledge originality, not an absolute absence proof.

value.rationale: Varying the distance of two boundary zeros of a cyclic Hardy generator is a natural approximation-design problem. The sharp optimized constant 1.791269..., compared with distinct fixed roots (2) and a coincident double root (4), reveals a genuine nonmonotone critical-scale benefit. The proof identifies a unique natural spacing and classifies an infinite recurrence of beating windows, rather than merely evaluating a known fixed-parameter Gram formula. The global minimizer has direct use as a parameter-selection benchmark for Hardy polynomial inverse approximation.
